title: Certificates of Deposit: term length, rate structure and renewal settings by tier
content:
## Scope

This quick reference covers the Certificates of Deposit line of Piedmont Crescent Bank and sets out, for every certificate tier, the length of one term, the rate structure, whether the certificate may renew automatically at maturity, the tier it renews into, the rate basis applied on renewal, and how far ahead of maturity the maturity notice is mailed. The tiers are listed in the bank's lineup order, from the shortest term to the longest.

## Definitions

- **Term length** is the length of one term of the certificate, stated as a whole number of calendar months.
- **Rate structure** is one of three kinds: *fixed*; *fixed, no penalty*; or *bump-up*.
- **Automatic renewal available** states whether the certificate may renew automatically at maturity.
- **Renewal tier** is the official tier name the certificate renews into when the owner makes no term change.
- **Renewal rate basis** is the rate applied on renewal. For every tier it is *published on the maturity date*, which means the standard APY and standard interest rate, as published on the maturity date, of the tier the certificate renews into, plus any bonuses then earned.
- **Maturity notice lead time** is the number of calendar days before the maturity date on which the maturity notice is mailed.

## Settings by tier

| Lineup order | Tier | Term length (calendar months) | Rate structure | Automatic renewal available | Renewal tier (no term change) | Renewal rate basis | Maturity notice mailed (calendar days before maturity) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 6-Month Certificate | 6 | Fixed | Yes | 6-Month Certificate | Published on the maturity date | 20 |
| 2 | 11-Month No-Penalty Certificate | 11 | Fixed, no penalty | Yes | 12-Month Certificate | Published on the maturity date | 20 |
| 3 | 12-Month Certificate | 12 | Fixed | Yes | 12-Month Certificate | Published on the maturity date | 20 |
| 4 | 18-Month Bump-Up Certificate | 18 | Bump-up | Yes | 18-Month Bump-Up Certificate | Published on the maturity date | 30 |
| 5 | 36-Month Certificate | 36 | Fixed | Yes | 36-Month Certificate | Published on the maturity date | 30 |
| 6 | 60-Month Certificate | 60 | Fixed | Yes | 60-Month Certificate | Published on the maturity date | 30 |

## Points of judgement

**Does every certificate renew into its own tier?**
No. Five tiers renew into the same tier when the owner makes no term change. The 11-Month No-Penalty Certificate is the exception: with no term change it renews into the 12-Month Certificate.

**Is a renewed term priced at the rate the certificate had before?**
No. On every tier the renewal rate basis is the standard APY and standard interest rate, as published on the maturity date, of the tier the certificate renews into, plus any bonuses then earned; the old term's rate does not carry over.

**Are the renewal tier and the renewal rate basis the same setting?**
No. The renewal tier names the tier the certificate renews into when the owner makes no term change. The renewal rate basis prices the new term at the published rates of whichever tier the certificate renews into.

**Which tiers have a thirty-day notice lead time?**
The 18-Month Bump-Up Certificate, the 36-Month Certificate and the 60-Month Certificate. The 6-Month, 11-Month No-Penalty and 12-Month Certificates have a twenty-day lead time.

## Illustrative notice dates (hypothetical maturity dates)

| Tier | Hypothetical maturity date | Lead time | Notice mailing date |
|---|---|---|---|
| 36-Month Certificate | 30 June | 30 calendar days | 31 May |
| 6-Month Certificate | 15 March of a year in which February has 28 days | 20 calendar days | 23 February |
